findings.note: The sentence "It says nothing about any other city or county." is an absence-of-law claim (SR-6). No statute_absence claim in the ledger supports it, and it also reaches beyond San Francisco's code. Remove the whole sentence.

The opening sentence "This is a San Francisco rule, not California law." comes before any rule is named, so "This" has no antecedent and the layer statement is not tied to its source (SR-2). Move it to directly follow the sentence naming San Francisco Housing Code section 351(a), for example "... Department of Building Inspection. This is a San Francisco rule, not California law." (the wording is carried by clm:1 to clm:4), and start the section with the 351(a) sentence.

required_actions: Delete: "It says nothing about any other city or county."
Move "This is a San Francisco rule, not California law." to follow the sentence that names San Francisco Housing Code section 351(a); do not open the section with it.

claim_checks.note: Obtain-report duty, first-sale exception and the owner or authorized agent match the 351(a) quote; attributed to San Francisco; the building meaning is carried by clm:2, which the unit also cites and states.
Definition with the 30-room hotel and motel exclusion matches 351(b); the unit says "For this rule", which is within the scope 'as used in this chapter'.

Delivery to the buyer or transferee before the sale is consummated matches the quote. NARROWER only by omitting the buyer's receipt filing and the unlawful-sale wording, which do not change what a seller must do before closing; the first-sale exception is stated in the preceding sentence (clm:1).

The no-representation-of-compliance statement matches the quote. NARROWER only by omitting no physical examination and compiled from City records, which does not change what a reader believes or does about the compliance point.

hedge_rulings.note: The layer statement is supported by the ledger wording of clm:1 to clm:4 (San Francisco rule, not California law), but as the opening sentence it has no antecedent. Attach it to the sentence naming section 351(a); no California-law claim is made, so no state-layer claim is needed.
